name: Lake Prairie Towne Crossing
summary: Lake Prairie Towne Crossing is a 246,440 square foot community shopping center prominently located at State Highway 360 and Camp Wisdom Road in Grand Prairie, Texas. With nearly 3,500 feet of highway frontage, the center serves as the retail hub for the surrounding Dallas-Fort Worth suburban communities.
demographics: Lake Prairie Towne Crossing serves a predominantly middle to upper-middle class suburban market in Grand Prairie, with median household incomes ranging from $80,382 in the 10-mile radius to $112,009 within 1 mile. The trade area encompasses over 819,000 residents within 10 miles, with strong representation of families and working professionals. The center attracts shoppers seeking convenient access to everyday retail and services along the heavily-trafficked State Highway 360 corridor, with visitors typically making multiple trips throughout the year for routine shopping needs.
description: Lake Prairie Towne Crossing is a prominent community shopping center strategically positioned at the corner of State Highway 360 and Camp Wisdom Road in Grand Prairie, Texas, serving the Dallas-Fort Worth metropolitan area. With nearly 3,500 feet of highway frontage along one of the region's busiest corridors, the center has established itself as the heart of retail activity in this rapidly growing suburban market. The 246,440 square foot development benefits from exceptional visibility and accessibility, drawing from a trade area of over 800,000 residents within a 10-mile radius. Managed by Kimco Realty Corporation, one of North America's largest publicly traded owners and operators of open-air shopping centers, Lake Prairie Towne Crossing offers a diverse mix of national retailers and local businesses catering to the everyday needs of Grand Prairie's middle to upper-middle class families. The center's location provides convenient access for the surrounding communities, with strong household incomes exceeding $112,000 within one mile and a daytime population of over 872,000 workers within the broader trade area.
